| 25 | An ordinary Spanish resident whose habitual residence falls in Navarra uses Navarra IRPF. A resident whose habitual residence falls in Bizkaia, Álava or Gipuzkoa uses that historical territory's IRPF. These are separate complete income-tax systems, not an additional autonomous-community percentage on top of the State scale. Apply the residence tests in order: greatest number of days during the tax period, counting temporary absences and the rebuttable habitual-home presumption; then principal centre of interests using the statutory income exclusions; then last declared IRPF residence. A Spanish resident spending no more than 183 days in Spain uses the principal economic-interest test. Keep the spouse/minor-child residence presumption and artificial residence-change rules in the applicable agreement. Mixed-territory joint returns follow the member with the largest taxable base calculated under that member's applicable law. Sources: Basque Economic Agreement arts 6 and 43 [Basque Economic Agreement, current consolidated law](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2002-9969); Navarra Economic Agreement arts 8–9 [Navarra Economic Agreement, current consolidated law](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1990-31117). | Who this applies to; current LF25; exact retained |
| 27 | Payroll withholding jurisdiction is a separate decision from the employee's final annual IRPF residence. The Basque art 7 employment-service/assigned-work-centre rules expressly cover mixed working locations, telework, overseas work and ships; public pensions use the recipient's habitual residence; directors use the paying entity's fiscal domicile and the prescribed mixed-corporate allocation. Apply the public-State-employer exception rather than moving all State payroll to a province. Navarra arts 10–16 contain its separate withholding points of connection. A resident's final return credits the properly attributable withholding even where a different administration collected it. [Basque Economic Agreement, current consolidated law](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2002-9969)[Navarra Economic Agreement, current consolidated law](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1990-31117) | Who this applies to; current LF27; exact retained |

| 71 | Under arts 62–66 classify employment, ordinary business income and other general income separately from savings income. Ordinary residential-property capital income belongs to the territorial savings basket under art 63(a), together with the specified financial-capital returns and disposal gains under art 63(b)–(c). This differs from ordinary common-territory rental-income classification. Calculate the property result using the local art 32 before placing it in that basket. Do not insert the State rental reduction or its actual-cost method into the foral property computation. [Bizkaia NF13/2013, current2026 consolidation](https://www.bizkaia.eus/documents/880307/15187815/ca_13_2013.pdf/ce52e403-4fca-9ef7-bf85-2505ba29f921?t=1784098584068)[Álava NF33/2013, current2026 consolidation](https://web.araba.eus/documents/d/araba/indice_norma-foral_irpf_cas-4-pdf)[Gipuzkoa NF3/2014,2026 consolidation](https://www.gipuzkoa.eus/documents/2456431/8.0759126E7/NF%203-2014%20(2026-0).pdf/8ab5c95c-3f89-8fdf-5cb8-01950e3983cc) arts 30–32,62–66. | Current LF98–102 savings-basket/property-classification rule; LF508–534 own Basque property method and LF536–551 separate Navarra method. No State rental reduction imported. |
| 73 | The savings-return and savings-disposal sub-baskets offset internally. A negative sub-basket carries to the same type of positive income for four following years; these provisions do **not** permit the common-territory 25% cross-offset between the two savings sub-baskets. Gipuzkoa has the specific ten-year qualifying innovative-company disposal-loss exception in art 66.1(b). Other non-business general gains/losses offset internally; a remaining negative gain balance offsets up to 25% of the qualifying positive general-income balance and then carries four years in statutory order. Economic-activity losses are kept separate and carry against positive business results for 30 years under art 65(b) and the incorporated corporate-tax conditions. Do not absorb them automatically against current salary. [Bizkaia NF13/2013, current2026 consolidation](https://www.bizkaia.eus/documents/880307/15187815/ca_13_2013.pdf/ce52e403-4fca-9ef7-bf85-2505ba29f921?t=1784098584068)[Álava NF33/2013, current2026 consolidation](https://web.araba.eus/documents/d/araba/indice_norma-foral_irpf_cas-4-pdf)[Gipuzkoa NF3/2014,2026 consolidation](https://www.gipuzkoa.eus/documents/2456431/8.0759126E7/NF%203-2014%20(2026-0).pdf/8ab5c95c-3f89-8fdf-5cb8-01950e3983cc) arts 65–66. | The base / General and savings baskets, reductions and pensions; current LF100; exact retained |
| 75 | Reduce the general base in the art 67 order: qualifying compensatory spouse pensions/non-child maintenance; eligible pension/EPSV contributions; joint-return reduction. Stop at zero. The unused art 69 compensatory-pension reduction can reduce savings under art 67.3. The general joint-return reduction is EUR 4,896 per return in all three territories for 2026, subject to the territorial family-unit definition and joint election. Navarra has a different joint-return method below. | 115 | Subtract the EUR 1,615 art 77 minoración **from general-scale quota**, with a zero floor, then add savings-scale quota. | 134 | For descendants, age 30 qualifies but age>30 fails unless disability/dependency conditions bring the person within the exception. The descendant's non-exempt annual income must not exceed the SMI; the other-family-unit income test and the descendant's own filing/no-filing requirement also apply. Prorate equally between equally close entitled ancestors; the closest degree has priority, with the statutory low-income fallback. Support under a qualifying judicial arrangement can substitute for cohabitation under the precise territorial art 79.5. Apply legal guardianship/fostering/representative-curatorship assimilations. These are quota deductions, not taxable-base allowances. [Bizkaia NF13/2013, current2026 consolidation](https://www.bizkaia.eus/documents/880307/15187815/ca_13_2013.pdf/ce52e403-4fca-9ef7-bf85-2505ba29f921?t=1784098584068)[Álava NF33/2013, current2026 consolidation](https://web.araba.eus/documents/d/araba/indice_norma-foral_irpf_cas-4-pdf)[Gipuzkoa NF3/2014,2026 consolidation](https://www.gipuzkoa.eus/documents/2456431/8.0759126E7/NF%203-2014%20(2026-0).pdf/8ab5c95c-3f89-8fdf-5cb8-01950e3983cc) art 79. | The base / Ordinary personal and family credits: territorial amounts matter; current LF268; exact retained |
| 136 | Ascendant credit requires continuous permanent full-year cohabitation or the qualifying payment of residential-home costs, the SMI/other-family-unit tests, and the ascendant's own filing test. Álava excludes centres in the foral/equivalent social-service network from the relevant paid-residence assimilation. Apply nearest-degree/equal-sharing rules. Álava increases basic descendant/ascendant credits by 15% for qualifying residence in a municipality with fewer than 4,000 people where the family's principal personal/social/health/education centre is genuinely situated; this does not automatically increase every supplemental child credit. [Bizkaia NF13/2013, current2026 consolidation](https://www.bizkaia.eus/documents/880307/15187815/ca_13_2013.pdf/ce52e403-4fca-9ef7-bf85-2505ba29f921?t=1784098584068)[Álava NF33/2013, current2026 consolidation](https://web.araba.eus/documents/d/araba/indice_norma-foral_irpf_cas-4-pdf)[Gipuzkoa NF3/2014,2026 consolidation](https://www.gipuzkoa.eus/documents/2456431/8.0759126E7/NF%203-2014%20(2026-0).pdf/8ab5c95c-3f89-8fdf-5cb8-01950e3983cc) arts 79–81. | The base / Ordinary personal and family credits: territorial amounts matter; current LF270; exact retained |
| 138 | For art 82 relatives the ordinary income ceiling is twice SMI, excluding exempt income, with the statutory fourth-degree and residential-cost conditions. The disabled/dependent person's own deduction takes priority unless the permitted election transfers it; split the transferred credit equally between entitled household members. Do not claim it twice. [Bizkaia NF13/2013, current2026 consolidation](https://www.bizkaia.eus/documents/880307/15187815/ca_13_2013.pdf/ce52e403-4fca-9ef7-bf85-2505ba29f921?t=1784098584068)[Álava NF33/2013, current2026 consolidation](https://web.araba.eus/documents/d/araba/indice_norma-foral_irpf_cas-4-pdf)[Gipuzkoa NF3/2014,2026 consolidation](https://www.gipuzkoa.eus/documents/2456431/8.0759126E7/NF%203-2014%20(2026-0).pdf/8ab5c95c-3f89-8fdf-5cb8-01950e3983cc) art 82. | The base / Ordinary personal and family credits: territorial amounts matter; current LF272; exact retained |
| 140 | Age-credit base is the positive general base plus savings base, with negative general base treated aszero and the art 69 compensatory-pension adjustment. For 20,000<base<30,000 use `393−0.0393×(base−20,000)` or `714−0.0714×(base−20,000)` respectively; at/above 30,000 the credit is zero. Widow credit similarly is `200−0.02×(base−20,000)` in that taper band. Ordinary family status is determined at year-end, or at death of the person creating entitlement, without a general day-by-day proration; specific employment/care credits have their own duration rules. [Bizkaia NF13/2013, current2026 consolidation](https://www.bizkaia.eus/documents/880307/15187815/ca_13_2013.pdf/ce52e403-4fca-9ef7-bf85-2505ba29f921?t=1784098584068)[Álava NF33/2013, current2026 consolidation](https://web.araba.eus/documents/d/araba/indice_norma-foral_irpf_cas-4-pdf)[Gipuzkoa NF3/2014,2026 consolidation](https://www.gipuzkoa.eus/documents/2456431/8.0759126E7/NF%203-2014%20(2026-0).pdf/8ab5c95c-3f89-8fdf-5cb8-01950e3983cc) arts 82 bis/83/83 quinquies,84. | The base / Ordinary personal and family credits: territorial amounts matter; current LF274; exact retained |
| 142 | Judicial child-support credit is 15% of exclusive qualifying payments to descendants up to second degree, capped per descendant at 30% of the corresponding **basic** art 79.1 credit. Gipuzkoa art 80 also expressly covers the qualifying regulator agreement approved judicially, before the court officer or in a notarial public instrument. This is not the State separate-scale child-support mechanism. | 165 | Under Bizkaia 93 bis, Álava 94 bis and Gipuzkoa 92 bis, unused main-home-rent credits carry five years. The specified descendant/purchase credits can also carry five years for under 36 contributors, who must remain under 36 when using that route. Use originating-year conditions/limits and the first year with sufficient quota, before the same current-year credit. Apply any additional named carry rules separately. For 2025–2029, however, the special voluntary-filer main-home-rent rule pays the unused rent credit where the taxpayer is not obliged to file but submits the return and has insufficient quota. Bizkaia uses the provisional assessment; Álava/Gipuzkoa refer to the return or provisional assessment. Offset the paid amount against pending rent credits so it is never refunded and carried twice. This is expressly authorised by BizkaiaDA 44, ÁlavaDA 42 and GipuzkoaDA 43; it is separate from ordinary carryforwards. Business investment, employee-share investment and new-company investment require the separate territorial corporate/credit methods; charitable giving follows the additional table below; the State 50% startup/80% gift figures do not apply automatically. [Bizkaia NF13/2013, current2026 consolidation](https://www.bizkaia.eus/documents/880307/15187815/ca_13_2013.pdf/ce52e403-4fca-9ef7-bf85-2505ba29f921?t=1784098584068)[Álava NF33/2013, current2026 consolidation](https://web.araba.eus/documents/d/araba/indice_norma-foral_irpf_cas-4-pdf)[Gipuzkoa NF3/2014,2026 consolidation](https://www.gipuzkoa.eus/documents/2456431/8.0759126E7/NF%203-2014%20(2026-0).pdf/8ab5c95c-3f89-8fdf-5cb8-01950e3983cc) | Current LF317 carry/refund priority and origin-year conditions; LF345–375 employee/newcompany carries and LF377–409 business-credit methods; charitable givingLF493–504. | 173 | Employment income is gross taxable money/benefits less the **exclusive** art 18 expense list: compulsory social-security/pension charges, essential mandatory professional-college dues capped 500/year under regulation 9, and direct employment-dispute legal costs capped 300/year. Current art 18 has no union-dues expense and no State 2,000 ordinary employment expense. Union dues instead have the 62.6 quota credit. Apply only the actual current 17.2 irregular/pension reduction and 17.3 exclusions for the relevant benefit; do not treat a periodic pension as a universally 40%-reduced lump sum. [Navarra DFL4/2008, current revision20April2026](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BON-n-2008-90013&p=20260420&tn=1) arts 13–19. | The base / Net income, baskets and reductions; current LF417; exact retained |
| 175 | Sole traders ordinarily use actual income less tax-deductible business expenses under 34–35. Simplified direct assessment applies, unless validly waived, where prior-year net turnover≤600,000 and the special method does not apply: table depreciation, no provisions/impairments, then deduct 5% of the positive net result. Special direct assessment covers qualifying agricultural/forestry/livestock/fishing turnover≤350,000 or specified recargo/simplified-VAT businesses≤250,000, with the linked-family/entity aggregation and VAT-election rules. Exclude provisions, impairment, depreciation and specified transport/agricultural-machine lease costs, then deduct 10% ordinarily,35% for qualifying agriculture/etc,45% road-freight IAE 722. This is a method on actual receipts/costs, not common-territory módulos. Apply 36(C)'s turnover definition, including grants/compensation where required, and the 2026 special-election rule to the actual election record. [Navarra DFL4/2008, current revision20April2026](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BON-n-2008-90013&p=20260420&tn=1) arts 34–36. | The base / Net income, baskets and reductions; current LF419; exact retained |
| 177 | General income art 53 comprises non-savings net income/imputations plus general non-disposal gains/losses. The latter negative balance offsets qualifying positive net income up to 25%, then carries four years. Savings art 54 has financial-capital and disposal-gain sub-baskets, including qualifying home-acquisition capital grants. Net internally, then cross-offset a negative sub-basket against a positive other sub-basket up to 25%; carry remainder four years in statutory order, oldest balances first. A general taxable-base loss carries four years under 56. Unlike the Basque method, ordinary Navarra savings does permit the art 54 cross-offset. [Navarra DFL4/2008, current revision20April2026](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BON-n-2008-90013&p=20260420&tn=1) arts 53–57. | The base / Net income, baskets and reductions; current LF423; exact retained |
| 179 | Apply art 55 pension and qualifying compensatory-spouse/non-child-maintenance reductions to the general base. Savings taxable base equals savings taxable income under 57; do not apply the repealed family-reduction spillover. The pension reduction is limited by the lower of eligible net-work/business income 30% (50% if the participant is older than 50) and the monetary limit: ordinary 1,500, eligible employer/employee increment 8,500 using employer matching (≤500 employer×2.5;500.01–1,500:1,250+.25×[E−500];>1,500:E; ratio 1 for employee gross>60,000 from that employer), plus the specified 4,250 own-account qualified-plan route, with 8,500 combined increment ceiling. The special employer scheme covering members but not the remaining workers has a 4,250 additional limit. Collective-dependency employer premium has its separate 5,000 ceiling. Respect financial limits and the five-year eligible excess carry. Separate spouse contribution:1,000 if spouse has no net work/business income or less than 8,500. Do not use the State spouse 8,000 threshold. [Navarra DFL4/2008, current revision20April2026](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BON-n-2008-90013&p=20260420&tn=1) art 55.1. | The base / Net income, baskets and reductions; current LF425; exact retained |

| 210 | Navarra joint assessment does not pool all spouses' income under one scale with a 4,896 reduction.
